subject: FintechCo — logging & redaction follow-up

Subject: FintechCo — logging & redaction follow-up

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we discussed on logging, retention, and redaction so your security team has something to review ahead of a deeper dive: 

Call recap (high level)
- You wanted clarity on what we persist in request/response logs (headers/body), how headers like Authorization / x-trace-id are handled, and whether trace IDs could be used to re-identify users.
- You asked about configurable retention windows and secure deletion, and whether logs can be disabled entirely for sensitive routes.
- You asked about data residency: hosted logs default to US regions but we have options for EU-only storage and Private deployments.

Redwood answers / options
- Default logging: we capture request metadata, non-sensitive headers, and model response metadata. By default we DO NOT persist full user-provided PII — we apply automatic PII redaction for common patterns (SSNs, credit card numbers, email addresses) to both request and response bodies.
- Header handling: sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) are always stripped or masked prior to persistence. Trace headers (x-trace-id, request-id) are by default hashed and stored as opaque tokens, not plain-text values.
- Trace IDs and linkability: trace IDs are not stored in a way that is directly linkable to customer user identifiers unless you explicitly send identifiable user IDs in the same payload. For additional assurance we can:
  - rotate/ephemeralize trace identifiers after a configurable window (default 7 days), or
  - disable trace-id persistence entirely for specific routes (configurable per-route).
- Retention: default retention is 90 days. For enterprise customers we support configurable retention (30 / 90 / 180 / 365) or an option to disable request/response logging entirely. Private deployments can be configured with zero retention or to keep logs only on-prem.
- Redaction controls: we support field-level masking (e.g., mask card_number, ssn), regex-based redaction rules, and built-in tokenizers for common PII. You can provide a list of fields to strip at the edge.
- Security controls: logs are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated/Private plans; access is audited. We are SOC 2 Type II and can provide a compliance package during the security review.

Attached: redwood-logging-redaction-overview.pdf (summary), sample_logging_config.json (example config showing per-route masking).

Next steps
1) Can you share the specific fields / headers you want redacted for the routes you mentioned?
2) If useful, we can do a 30–45m security deep dive next week — Dev (cc'd) will join to walk the config and demo masked logs.

Thanks — I can also share a sanitized sample log export if that helps.

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from the security side so we can triage internally: 

1) Trace IDs: you mentioned hashing + rotation. Can you confirm whether hashed trace IDs remain stable for the lifetime of a retention window (i.e., could we correlate events across days using the same hashed id)? If so, we need to understand the correlation risk. Could you provide an option that completely strips trace IDs before persistence?

2) Re-identification risk: do you perform any linkages server-side (e.g., joins to customer-provided user ids) for debugging/ops that would persist alongside logs? We need a clear statement that logs stored in hosted will not be enriched with identifiable user attributes unless the customer opts in.

3) Data residency: can you confirm hosted logs for our account will be stored in the US only? We also need to see the SOC 2 snapshot and a redaction guide we can give to legal.

4) Retention & deletion SLA: what is the SLA for permanent deletion if we request a purge? We need this in writing for procurement.

If you can share a short config example that shows: (a) stripping x-trace-id, (b) masking any field named card_number and ssn, and (c) retention set to 30 days, that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to take a short call next week.

—Priya
Head of Security Operations, FintechCo
priya.reddy@fintechco.com

On Sat, 12 Sep 2026 at 09:18, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@fintechco.com> wrote:
> 1) Trace IDs: you mentioned hashing + rotation. Can you confirm whether hashed trace IDs remain stable for the lifetime of a retention window (i.e., could we correlate events across days using the same hashed id)?
>
> 2) Re-identification risk: do you perform any linkages server-side (e.g., joins to customer-provided user ids) for debugging/ops?

Hi Priya — quick answers and a sample config. Happy to walk through live next week.

Trace IDs / correlation
- By default we store a hashed trace token that remains stable for the configured retention window to allow tracing of a request group across retries. Hashing is one-way (SHA256 with a keyed salt) and the raw trace id is not retrievable from stored logs.
- If you prefer zero correlation we offer two options: (A) strip trace headers entirely at the edge (no token stored), or (B) store only ephemeral tokens that are rotated every 24 hours. We can enable either on a per-route basis.

Server-side joins / enrichment
- We do NOT enrich hosted logs with customer user identifiers unless you explicitly configure the connector to attach them (this is an opt-in operator action). Debugging workflows that require ID joins are only available for Dedicated/Private customers under strict RBAC and audit controls.

Retention & deletion SLA
- Deletion/purge requests for hosted logs: standard SLA is 72 hours to remove the data from primary stores and 30 days for complete removal from backups. For Dedicated/Private we can provide custom SLAs and immediate deletion within the cluster.

Data residency
- Hosted US accounts store logs in US regions by default (we can lock to us-east-1). For EU-only storage we use separate controls and dedicated EU buckets.

Sample config (attached file: sample_logging_config.json) — key lines shown here as an example:

# sample snippet (yaml-like)
per_route:
  /v1/payments:
    log_persistence: true
    retention_days: 30
    strip_headers: [\"Authorization\", \"Cookie\", \"x-trace-id\"]
    field_masking:
      - name: card_number
        method: regex_mask
      - name: ssn
        method: full_mask

If you want, I can generate a sanitized sample log export that demonstrates the redaction in action. Attaching a couple of files: redwood-redaction-examples.json (sanitized samples) and the earlier overview PDF.

Happy to hop on a call — Marissa, can you share times next week?

Thanks,
